newsitem.title: ITALY: Turin fire contained, historic shroud safe.
newsitem.headline: Turin fire contained, historic shroud safe.

text.p: A fire which destroyed part of this northern city's cathedral was under control and the historic Turin shroud, housed in the 15th century building, was safe, a fire officer said on Saturday.

A section of the adjoining royal palace was also wrecked by the night-time blaze. Shortly before the fire took hold, United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan attended a gala dinner in the building along with numerous local dignitaries.

"The fire is under control but we're still working very hard to minimise the risks," Michele Ferraro, head of the fire rescue service, told Reuters. He added it was still too soon to say how the blaze started.

Security guards said the fire began at the back of the cathedral, in the Guarini chapel. The shroud, a piece of cloth imprinted with the image of a man's body that many Roman Catholic believers take to be the figure of Christ after his crucifixion, was stored behind bullet-proof glass in the chapel.

Firemen smashed the glass with a sledge hammer and carried the religious relic to safety. Ferraro said the chapel, which was under restoration, was completely gutted, while there had been extensive damage to one floor of the royal palace.

The U.N. Secretary General is in Turin to inaugurate a staff college of the International Labour Organisation later on Saturday. A police official said there was no indication that the blaze had been started deliberately.
